claim_citation.text: | Offline Tier C auth tokens | Implemented | security/offline_tokens.py, action_dispatcher.py, state/store.py, tests/test_offline_tokens_v2_vectors.py | Two formats. A v2 token (`offline-tokens/v2`) binds one open proposal, device, exact action, target and commissioned zone, is signed in the `ori.offline_token.v2` domain, is read by exact integer `token_version` from the JSON number token before any signature is verified, refuses a member named twice at any depth, and is claimed inside the approval commit so a spent token and an unadmitted approval never exist apart. A v1 token approves no physical action at any tier and no Tier C action; it remains the local-console approval for a host-state Tier B action that requires approval, signature-verified, device/action-bound, expiry-checked and replay-protected. The signing-domain corpus is verified against real Ed25519 signatures under a published test key that the runtime refuses as a trust anchor. |

hunks.summary: The status note beside the rendered Status paragraph said v1 is the format the runtime verifies; it verifies v2, and v1 only for actions that are neither physical nor Tier C. Descriptive; it changes no conforming output, accepted input, transition, rejection, ordering, authority or interpretation.

notes: A token bound to one open Tier C proposal, device, action, target and commissioned zone, signed in its own domain. The runtime's verifier claims this version from its claiming merge; no issuer implements it yet. v1 is the shipped legacy format.
